title: 'Breaking Bad' actor and disability advocate RJ Mitte dies
summary: RJ Mitte said his lived experience with cerebral palsy was an asset for his role as Walter White's son Flynn on "Breaking Bad."

image.caption: RJ Mitte had key roles in 'Breaking Bad,' 'Switched at Birth' and 'Guardians of Justice'Image: Gage Skidmore/ZUMA/picture alliance

blocks.text: American actor RJ Mitte, whose lived experience with cerebral palsy was channeled into a key role in "Breaking Bad," died on Monday at the age of 34.
"It is with profound ​sadness that we share the tragic passing of beloved actor, philanthropist, and passionate disability rights ​advocate RJ Mitte," his management agency said in a statement.
No other details about the circumstances of his death were given.

In addition to his breakout role in in "Breaking Bad" and later credits including "Switched at Birth" and "Guardians of Justice," Mitte also served as an ambassador for United Cerebral Palsy and Shriners Hospitals for Children.

In "Breaking Bad," Mitte played Walter White Jr., the son of Bryan Cranston's character, chemistry teacher-turned-meth dealer Walter White. Mitte's character used crutches and spoke with a slur, and gained greater prominence as the series progressed.
"Mitte brought authenticity to the role and built ​a platform on disability awareness and inclusion," the statement said.
"Breaking Bad" ran from 2008 until 2023. With 16 Emmy awards, it's often cited by critics as one of the best television dramas of all time.

Shortly after the series wrapped up, Mitte told the Associated Press that his disability and the surrounding struggles with physical therapy, family problems and exorbitant medical bills — all of which featured in the show — made him better in his role.
"You develop a different mentality and you develop a different look at how the world sees you and how you see the world," he said in 2024.
"You're able to use that. And I think it's an asset instead of something that would hinder," Mitte added.
